name: htpdate
desc: Synchronize time with remote web servers
why: Sets the clock by reading HTTP Date headers from web servers, a neat back door into time sync without NTP.

brief.what_it_is: htpdate is a command-line tool that sets the local system clock by reading the Date header from remote web servers over HTTP, rather than using NTP. According to the Homebrew formula description, it synchronizes time with remote web servers, and the executable is named htpdate. I could not read the project's own documentation, so the details of inputs and outputs are not confirmed.
brief.why_it_exists: Not confirmed. The project homepage at vervest.org/htp/ is a redirect to GitHub, and I could not reach the README, so I have no author framing to quote.
brief.install_notes: Installed via Homebrew (brew install htpdate). No further install, configuration, or first-run details were available because the README was not reached.
brief.standout: The scout note describes it as a way to set the clock from HTTP Date headers without NTP, which is an unusual approach. I have not verified this against the project's own documentation.
brief.caveats: The homepage https://www.vervest.org/htp/ redirects to GitHub but the response did not include the target URL. I guessed https://github.com/vervest/htpdate and it returned HTTP 404, so the repository location is unconfirmed. Nothing about platform support, licensing, or maintenance could be checked. The description above relies only on the Homebrew formula text and the scout note.
